reasoning_quality_informational.v1_root_problem: Billing dispute tickets have roughly doubled since August 2026 (from ~600/month in Jun-Jul to 1180-1260/month in Aug-Sep, E-06), and the dominant driver is a billing import/validation defect producing incorrect bills on ACTUAL-read accounts rather than ticket-response speed (E-01 shows response times within SLA) or estimated-read substitution from field/AMI issues (E-04 shows disputed bills are dominated by ACTUAL reads, 1785 vs 1240 ESTIMATED, and E-03 rules out a tariff change). The pattern is consistent with H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE: a change to billing import validation rules around August introduced systematic errors on correctly-read bills, which has not yet been directly confirmed against the billing-config rule change log.
reasoning_quality_informational.v2_root_problem: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled since August 2026 (610/590 per month Jun/Jul to 1180/1260 Aug/Sep, E-06). The confirmed mechanism behind the ESTIMATED-read dispute population (1240, matching E-04) is validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 (E-13), which compares raw AMI register values to 12-month m3 history with unit_scaling='none' and so misclassifies valid high-consumption reads from v4.2-firmware meters (reporting in 0.1 m3 units, not m3, E-14) as anomalous, rejecting 1184 of them at billing import and forcing estimate substitution (E-12); whether the same rule/unit mismatch also explains the larger ACTUAL-read population (1785, E-04) is not yet established.
reasoning_quality_informational.ideal_final_problem: BV-17 validation rejects valid firmware-v4.2 AMI reads (unit-scale mismatch on H-MDMS-BILL) and substitutes estimates.
